title: Development and validation of in-situ and laboratory X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectroscopy methods for moss biomonitoring of metal pollution
author: Messager, Davies, et al.

steps.title: Prepare metal‑free tools
steps.instruction: Use plastic petri dishes, plastic forceps, ceramic‑blade scissors, powder‑free nitrile gloves, and pure‑aluminum oven dishes; wash all instruments with soap, rinse with 95 % ethanol, then with distilled water between uses.

steps.title: Clean moss samples
steps.instruction: With sterilized plastic forceps, remove dead tissue, bark, insects, and any attached litter from the moss; do not wash the material.

steps.title: Dry moss shoots
steps.instruction: Place cleaned moss shoots in pure‑aluminum oven dishes and dry in an oven at 40 °C for 24 h.

steps.title: Grind dried moss to powder
steps.instruction: Manually grind the dried shoots in an unglazed mortar and pestle until homogeneous, adding liquid nitrogen as needed to keep the material brittle.

steps.title: Weigh and aliquot powder
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.5 g of the powdered moss, place it in a glass vial (mix material from all mats of a given tree beforehand to average micro‑variations).

steps.title: Pelletize powder
steps.instruction: Load the 0.5 g powder into a 13 mm diameter evacuable pellet die (Specac P/N GS03000, UK); press with 7 t for 1 min using a manual 15‑ton hydraulic press (Atlas™ model, P/N GS15011, Specac, UK), ensuring pressure builds up and releases gradually over ~10 s; do not add binding powder.

steps.title: Transfer pellet to XRF instrument
steps.instruction: Using powder‑free nitrile gloves, release the pellet from the die and place it on top of the pXRF instrument nozzle; ensure the pXRF analyzer is on the benchtop with a protective lead cover, an Ultralene gridded window, and connected to a laptop.

steps.title: Acquire XRF spectra
steps.instruction: Take an assay from each side of the pellet; acquire spectra for 120 s (≈110 s live time) per side with the instrument set to 40 keV voltage, 25 µA anode current, and no vacuum.

steps.title: Store pellets post‑measurement
steps.instruction: After measurement, keep the pellets in a desiccator containing gypsum (calcium sulfate) grains.
